Title: BC-11 copy review: the Speak Your Mind disclosure line, as shipped
What this is: Your BC-11 ruling asked for the disclosure to be drafted this session, marked for your review as COPY, and shipped as drafted meanwhile. It ships as: 'What you write may be shared - without a name, because we don't hold one - with campaigns, organizations, and researchers working to understand what people want.' Three things in it are load-bearing and worth checking: it says MAY rather than will, because a commitment not honoured on every instance is worse than a reserved right; it gives the REASON there is no name inside the sentence, because anonymously is a promise and we-don't-hold-one is a checkable fact; and it names the buyer classes out loud at the moment of typing. The framing above the box reads 'What would you say if [the body] were standing in front of you?' and the placeholder is 'What would you want to say?'. Change any of it and the words live in lib/speak/copy.ts.

Title: BC-11 held queue: severe Speak Your Mind rows are waiting for you, and T05 is the reason there is nowhere to read them
What this is: Rule 4 of your BC-11 ruling is built: nothing typed into Speak Your Mind is ever auto-forwarded, and content the triage reads as a threat or as menacing is stored with review_state HELD and excluded from everything. What does not exist is the surface where you READ that queue and act on it - which is exactly what T05 says about the abuse policy generally. This row links the two: the HOLD half now has a concrete first surface, and the REVIEW half is still yours to unblock. T05 stays open and only you close it. The tiers are docs/abuse-policy.md's own T1/T2/T3, not new ones, and the rules that decide are lib/speak/triage.ts with the harsh-political-speech cases planted in the test so over-filtering fails the build.

Title: OFF-3 photo: Dr. Gabriel Trujillo, TUSD superintendent - not sourced this session, and the reason is worth your call
What this is: OFF-3 asked for the superintendent's photo from the TUSD site, queued for your review under the photo rules, with the rest of the board swept alongside. NOT DONE this session and reported as not done rather than smoothed. Two things you may want to rule on. First, the four-door rule: a district's own site publishing a portrait of its own superintendent is door 2, an official government-published portrait, and TUSD is not a .gov host - so whether door 2 reaches a school district's own domain is your call and not a session's. Second, the app spells him Gabriel Trujillo; the 8/24 brief dictated Gabrielle. The naming rule says the app's spelling is authoritative, so nothing was changed - but if the app is wrong, that is a data fix and it wants your word first. The board's other five members already carry portraits; he is the one initials circle on that card.

Title: The rail and the floaters share one column, and 58% is a judgement that wants a second look
What this is: LAY-4 puts Who Governs Here and the meetings count in a floating region beneath the rail, and both live in one fixed flex column so they cannot overlap at any viewport. At 1440x900 the rail wants 662px and the who-governs card wants 350px or more against 876px of column, so they do not both fit and something is always scrolling. The rail is capped at 58% of the column: at 70% the card had 100px, less than its own header. Both scroll internally so nothing is unreachable either way, and WGH-6 is the real answer - clicking Who Governs Here minimizes the rail and the card takes the whole column. The number decides what a reader sees BEFORE they choose, and it is the kind of call worth looking at on a real screen.

Title: A meeting entry repeats the card title where the source publishes one name for every sitting
What this is: MTG-6 titles a venue card with the body and MTG-7 puts the sitting's own name on the entry beneath. Where a source publishes a DIFFERENT bodyName per sitting - Tucson Unified does, with names like GOVERNING BOARD AGENDA SPECIAL MEETING - the entry carries something distinct and it reads well. Where a source publishes ONE name for every sitting, as Tucson Parks and Recreation does, the entry repeats the card title. Sean's own reference capture 12-01-44 shows the same repetition and he marked only the jurisdiction prefix, so nothing was changed here. Worth a look on a real card: the honest options are to drop the entry title where it equals the card title, or to leave it as the anchor for the date and the agenda link.
